2	
3	An ocean-modeling group is post-processing a tracer field from a global
4	finite-volume calculation. The supplied grid is represented as several
5	logically rectangular faces that meet at rotated edges. Interpolation and
6	differencing across those edges are part of the same diagnostic workflow used
7	to form transport and mixing budgets.

9	The workflow completes and returns finite arrays, but a connected padding call

11	positions then no longer come from the neighboring face declared by the

13	even though the physical grid and field are unchanged. A connected edge is a
14	geometric interface: padding must preserve the input dimension order, and for a
15	scalar face-label field every non-corner halo position in that layout must have
16	the label of the declared neighboring face, independent of process hash seed.

21	supported by the project. The repair must remain correct for other connected

1	# Scientific background for task 045
2	
3	This task uses the finite-volume post-processing model described by the bundled
4	xgcm paper and documentation.  Xgcm operates on data from general circulation
5	models, where a physical domain may be represented by several logically
6	rectangular faces.  Variables may also live at different positions on a
7	staggered grid.  Interpolation and differencing therefore need both the local
8	axis position and the topology connecting one face to another.
9	
10	## Finite-volume meaning
11	
12	Finite-volume methods associate values with cells or cell faces and evaluate
13	fluxes and differences across shared interfaces. A connected multi-face grid
14	is only a representation of one physical domain: an interface shared by two
15	faces must expose the same physical data from either side, after applying the
16	orientation encoded by the topology. A local operation at that interface
17	should not change the physical interpretation of a valid representation of the
18	data.
19	
20	For a scalar field, a topological connection transfers the scalar value and
21	may reverse the tangential index order when the two local axes have opposite
22	orientation.  For a vector component, the same geometric reorientation may
23	also change the sign of the component.  These are properties of the physical
24	grid, not choices of a particular array library.
25	
26	## Why halo values matter
27	
28	Post-processing code often creates a small halo around each face before calling
29	a difference or interpolation operator.  At an interior interface, the halo
30	must contain the neighboring face's edge values; at an external boundary, the
31	configured boundary condition applies instead.  A wrong halo can still be
32	finite and have the expected shape while producing a wrong transport,
33	divergence, vorticity, or mixing diagnostic.
34	
35	The supplied source and documents describe the `face_connections` structure,
36	axis positions, rotated connections, boundary padding, and the relationship
37	between interpolation and differencing.  They are intentionally broader than
38	the one public field and do not prescribe a source-level repair.
39	
40	## References
41	
42	The full xgcm JOSS paper is included in `source/paper.md` with its bibliography
43	and figures.  The public source also includes the xgcm grid-topology and
44	boundary-condition documentation, the project citation and license, and the
45	original surrounding tests.  The Arakawa C-grid background and finite-volume
46	references in the paper are the intended scientific oracle for this task.
47

140	# Some helper functions for the connections padding
141	def _prepad_right_left_same_axis(da, boundary_width, fill_value, x="x", y="y"):
142	    # Manually put together the data
143	    face_0 = da.isel(face=0)
144	    face_1 = da.isel(face=1)
145	
146	    # pad on each side except on the connected side
147	    face_0_padded = face_0.pad(
148	        **{
149	            x: (boundary_width["X"][0], 0),
150	            y: (boundary_width["Y"][0], boundary_width["Y"][1]),
151	            "mode": "constant",
152	            "constant_values": fill_value,
153	        }
154	    )
155	
156	    face_1_padded = face_1.pad(
157	        **{
158	            x: (0, boundary_width["X"][1]),
159	            y: (boundary_width["Y"][0], boundary_width["Y"][1]),
160	            "mode": "constant",
161	            "constant_values": fill_value,
162	        }
163	    )
164	    return face_0_padded, face_1_padded

301	):
302	    """Regression test for https://github.com/xgcm/xgcm/issues/704.
303	
304	    When the vector components are dask-backed, padding splits the core
305	    dimension into boundary chunks, so the operation goes through
306	    ``_rechunk_to_merge_in_boundary_chunks``. That helper used to assume the
307	    argument was always a ``DataArray`` and raised
308	    ``AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'variable'`` when handed
309	    the ``{"X": u}`` vector-component dict (see the traceback in #704). Here we
310	    keep the inputs lazy (single chunk per core dim) so the result must match
311	    the numpy path exactly.
312	    """
313	    pytest.importorskip("dask")
314	
315	    grid = Grid(ds, face_connections=ds_face_connections_x_to_y)
316	
317	    # Keep the components lazy with a single chunk per core dim. This mirrors
318	    # the #704 scenario: map_overlap stays False, but padding still chunks the
319	    # core dim, exercising _rechunk_to_merge_in_boundary_chunks.
320	    u = ds.u.chunk()
321	    v = ds.v.chunk()
322	
323	    vector_out = getattr(grid, method)(
324	        {"X": u, "Y": v},
325	        to="center",
326	        boundary="fill",
327	        fill_value=100,
328	    )
329	    u_c = vector_out["X"]
330	
331	    # The result should stay on the dask path.
332	    assert u_c.chunks is not None
333	
334	    # Values must match the numpy path: first point is normal, last point picks
335	    # up the rotated neighbour across the face connection.
336	    if method == "interp_2d_vector":
337	        np.testing.assert_allclose(
338	            u_c.data[0, 0, :], 0.5 * (ds.u.data[0, 0, :] + ds.u.data[0, 1, :])

345	            u_c.data[0, 0, :], ds.u.data[0, 1, :] - ds.u.data[0, 0, :]
346	        )

180	
181	Because of the diversity of different model grid topologies, xgcm tries to
182	avoid making assumptions about the nature of the connectivity between faces.

186

189	    {<FACE DIMENSION VALUE>:
190	         {'<AXIS NAME>': (<LEFT CONNECTION>, <RIGHT CONNECTION>),
191	          ...}
192	    ...
193	}
194	```
195	
196	`<LEFT CONNECTION>>` and `<RIGHT CONNECTION>` are either `None` (for no
197	connection) or a three element tuple with the following contents
198

201	```

203	`<FACE DIMENSION VALUE>` tells which face this face is connected to.
204	`<AXIS NAME>` tells which axis on that face is connected to this one.
205	`<REVERSE CONNECTION>` is a boolean specifying whether the connection is
206	"reversed". A normal (non reversed) connection connects the right edge of one
207	face to the left edge of another face. A reversed connection connects
208	left to left, or right to right.
